Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 72, verse 1–2:

Naming of the Surah

• It is called Al-Jinn (The Jinn), because it mentions some of the states, statements and wondrous accounts of the jinn, and their relationship with humankind.

From the Objectives of the Surah

• To establish a miracle (karamah) for the Prophet (ﷺ), that his call reached the jinn, who believed immediately upon hearing the Qur'an, called their people to faith, devoted worship exclusively to Allah the Exalted, and declared Him free of any consort or offspring.

• To refute those who fabricate lies against Allah without knowledge and deny the Resurrection; to nullify the worship of what is worshipped besides Allah among the jinn; to show that the heavens are guarded against the jinn's eavesdropping; to nullify soothsaying (kihanah) and the claim that knowledge of the unseen reaches anyone other than the Messengers, whom Allah informs of whatever He wills.

[Tafsir]

Say, O Messenger: Allah has revealed to me that a group of the jinn listened to my recitation of the Qur'an. When they heard it, they said to their people: "Indeed, we have heard a wondrous Qur'an in its eloquence and clarity, in its wisdom, its rulings and its reports, which calls to the truth and guidance. So we have believed in this Qur'an and acted upon it, and we will never associate anyone in worship with our Lord, who created us."

[Tafsir]

Say, O Messenger: Allah has revealed to me that a group of the jinn listened to my recitation of the Qur'an. When they heard it, they said to their people: "Indeed, we have heard a wondrous Qur'an in its eloquence and clarity, in its wisdom, its rulings and its reports, which calls to the truth and guidance. So we have believed in this Qur'an and acted upon it, and we will never associate anyone in worship with our Lord, who created us."
And [we believe] that the majesty and greatness of our Lord are exalted; He has not taken a wife nor a son.
And that our foolish one—namely Iblis—used to speak about Allah, exalted is He, a statement far removed from truth and rightness, namely the claim that He has a consort and a son.
And we had thought that no one would ever lie against Allah, Exalted is He, neither among mankind nor among the jinn, by attributing a consort and offspring to Him.

And that there were men among mankind who sought refuge with men among the jinn, so the jinn increased them in burden (rahaqa) by their seeking refuge with them, out of fear, terror and dread. This seeking of refuge in other than Allah, which Allah condemned in the people of ignorance (jahiliyyah), is from the greater shirk (al-shirk al-akbar), which Allah will not forgive except through sincere repentance (tawbah nasuh) from it. And in the verse there is a severe warning against resorting to sorcerers, charlatans and their like.
And that the disbelievers among mankind thought, just as you (O assembly of jinn) thought, that God, exalted is He, would never resurrect anyone after death.
"And we (the jinn) sought to reach the heaven to listen to its inhabitants, but we found it filled with many angels guarding it, and with flaming meteors which are hurled at whoever comes near it."

And we used to sit in places of the heavens to listen in on its news. But whoever tries to eavesdrop now will find a shooting star lying in wait for him, which burns him and destroys him. In these two verses is a refutation of the claims of sorcerers and charlatans, who claim knowledge of the unseen and deceive the weak-minded with their lies and fabrications.
And we, the jinn, do not know: does Allah intend to bring harm upon the people of the earth, or does He intend for them good and guidance?
And among us are the righteous and the God-fearing, and among us are others who are below that: disbelievers and wrongdoers. We were divided into different sects and paths.

We have come to know with certainty that Allah is able over us, and that we are in His grip and under His authority. So we cannot escape Him if He wills something for us, wherever we may be, and we will not be able to flee from His punishment by escaping to the sky, if He wills harm for us.

And as for us, when we heard the Qur'an, we believed in it and acknowledged that it is the truth from Allah. So whoever believes in his Lord will not fear any diminution of his good deeds, nor any injustice that would add to his evil deeds.

And among us are those who submit to God in obedience, and among us are those who are unjust and deviate, who have turned away from the path of truth. Whoever submits and surrenders to God in obedience, those are the ones who sought the path of truth and right and strove to choose it, so God guided them to it. As for those who deviated from the path of Islam, they became fuel for Hell.

And the mosques are for the worship of Allah alone, so do not worship anything else along with Him within them, and devote your supplication and worship to Him alone in them. For the mosques were built only so that Allah alone be worshipped in them, to the exclusion of anyone else. The verse contains an obligation to keep the mosques free from everything that mars sincerity (ikhlas) towards Allah, and from everything that departs from following His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ).
And when Muhammad (ﷺ) stood up worshipping his Lord, the jinn nearly became massed around him, piled upon one another, from the intensity of their crowding to hear the Qur'an from him.
Say, O Messenger, to these disbelievers: I only worship my Lord alone, and I do not associate anyone with Him in worship.

Say, O Messenger, to them: "I do not have the power to repel harm from you, nor to bring you benefit." Say: "No one will save me from the punishment of Allah if I disobey Him, and I will not find any refuge other than Him to flee to from His punishment. But I have the (duty) to convey to you from Allah what He has commanded me to convey to you, and His message with which He has sent me to you. And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger, and turns away from the religion of Allah, his recompense is the Fire of Hell, where he will remain forever, never to leave it."

**Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 72, verse 24:**

Until, when the disbelievers see the punishment they have been promised, they will know, when it befalls them, who is weaker in helper and supporter, and fewer in soldiers.

Say, O Messenger, to these polytheists: I do not know whether the punishment you have been promised is near in time, or whether my Lord will appoint for it a lengthy term. He, glory be to Him, knows the unseen that is hidden from sight, and He does not reveal His unseen to anyone of His creation, except whomever He has chosen for His message and approved. Indeed, He informs them of some of the unseen, and He sends angels before the Messenger and behind him to guard him from the jinn, lest they steal away (the revelation) and whisper it to the soothsayers, so that the Messenger ﷺ may know that the messengers before him were upon the same course as his in conveying the truth with sincerity, that he has been protected just as they were protected from the jinn, and that Allah, glory be to Him, has encompassed with His knowledge all that is with them, outwardly and inwardly, of laws, rulings and other things, nothing of which escapes Him, and that He, exalted is He, has enumerated everything in number, so nothing of it is hidden from Him.
